decisions.why: The task's own subject (a red make done on a stale derived file), filed as performance work under FR-013 and the GM's 2026-11-20 'prioritize performance improvements'; it moves an existing check earlier, adds no behavior beyond refusing a stale file the gate already refuses.

decisions.summary: checks/documents/derived_quick.rs pins the quick recipe to preflight's DERIVED table; a derived target quick does not check, or one the table does not know, is red naming the line to add
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested behavior only: with the derived lines deleted from the spec the pin has nothing left to check (GM 2026-09-20 on checks that make the asked thing keep happening). FR-012 red-first is honored in the table.

decisions.summary: reviews prereq standing names a unit whose last PASS/NEEDS-WORK is carried to the sheet as just snapshotted and whose every open finding (not review-accepted) is nitpick, outside or confirmation; review-tree.sh prints it answered and leaves it out of the dispatch count
decisions.why: Implements the GM's approved 2026-11-23 rules 'only factual findings cascade' and 'settled choices stay settled' and his 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies' for building reviews; measured first (4 byte-identical sheets dispatched anyway), with one-shot labels on the figures.

decisions.summary: a fixed error or questionable finding owes its round even on an unchanged sheet (e.g. fixed in the docs)
decisions.why: An error or questionable finding is a factual one; 'only factual findings cascade' is the GM's rule, so a factual fix owing a round is the rule applied, not a carve-out from it. The sheet being unchanged does not show the fix was right.

decisions.summary: a finding of no or an unknown severity owes a round, failing closed as T188 does
decisions.why: The standing rule exempts only findings shown to be non-factual; a finding whose class is unknown cannot be shown so, and failing closed keeps the GM's 'only factual findings cascade' from passing an unclassified factual finding.

decisions.summary: a nitpick fixed on the sheet owes only a change-scoped, adversarial building-review of the edit (make review-fixed UNIT= FINDING=, the kept reviewed sheet, T189's before/after pairs); a clean SCOPE=change verdict (PASS, every finding minor, gate not red) is carried by carried/answered/standing/checkpoint/push review gate
decisions.why: Directly the GM's words 'make only the smallest possible changes perhaps with some kind of adversarial subagent review process' and the approved rule 're-reviews scoped to the change'. The plan says plainly the saving is unmeasured and the rule is the GM's, which is correct framing.

decisions.summary: an error or questionable finding fixed on the sheet is refused by make review-fixed and owes the full round, not a change-scoped one
decisions.why: In tension with 're-reviews scoped to the change', which the section itself applies to building reviews, so it is ruled. Legitimate on the GM's own words: 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies. And it might be that when we are cascading, we are only interested in factual inaccuracies' - the scoped route he proposed was for the small, non-factual edits, and a factual fix is the class he said matters. Purpose test: the oscillation the GM described was rounds driven by style findings; under this same section any nitpick the full round raises then stands (T199-standing) and, if fixed, owes only a scoped round, so the full round cannot restart the oscillation. Nor is it a defect left: a full review after a real-flaw fix is not a wrong outcome. Resting this on the request's words, not on T199's task line, which the bundle does not carry.

decisions.summary: a change-scoped round that is not clean (not PASS, a finding above minor, or its gate red) owes the full round
decisions.why: The adversarial scoped round exists to catch an edit that did more than the named fix or made something wrong; when it finds that, the change is no longer the small one the GM's scoped route covers, so falling back is the route working, not an exception to it.

decisions.summary: a verdict recorded before T199 (no kept reviewed sheet hashing to its content_key) owes the full round
decisions.why: Physically impossible otherwise: the change-scoped round reviews the diff between the sheet the verdict read and the sheet now, and before T199 the reviewed sheet was not kept (the snapshot is replaced by the next make verify), so there is no 'change' to scope a review to. It lapses on its own as verdicts are re-recorded.

decisions.summary: stalls::in_progress names a builder only while its task is in progress: box open, started since its last landing (task-starts row after the last land end, or the active mark), not held by waits, not held by name by a binding ruling (holds::named), its feature not set down at or after its last start
decisions.why: The GM approved (2026-11-23) a periodic check that 'speaks only when it is idle with actionable work and respects binding rulings and set-downs'. A parked (set down since start), waiting, held-by-name, landed or never-started builder is not actionable work; naming it with a wake command is the wrong outcome the request was filed to end. Each condition carries a clause of the approved proposal; none narrows it.

decisions.summary: A ruling that holds NEW work (holds::held) does not hold a task already started, and a set-down BEFORE the task's start does not either: T184's builder, started 19:22:55Z under 451's new-work hold and after an 11:06:29Z set-down, is still named
decisions.why: 'Respects binding rulings and set-downs' is honored to each ruling's own reach: a hold on new work holds the tasks not yet started (the plan's statement of holds::held and T183; rulings.md carries no ruling text, so the hold's scope is taken from the plan). The request itself describes the offending block as a 'builder slot is free' prompt under a ruling 'that held new work' - i.e. a prompt to START work; naming a live builder of an already-started task starts nothing. A set-down before a later start is superseded by that start (active's own test). No ruling or set-down is overridden, so nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: WAIT_SECS 600 -> 2,400 s (MONITOR_SECS 1,800 measured + STALL_SECS 600 GUESS), so a watch that runs its full 30 minutes and ends unheard is named within one check
decisions.why: Fixes a defect in the approved check: a builder stalled after a Monitor that outlived the 600 s wait was never named, i.e. the check stayed silent while idle with actionable work, contrary to the request. A constant change serving the request.

decisions.summary: The Idle hook entry's timeout 960 -> 2,760 s (the two waits + 60 s reads, a CONVENTION), pinned by the_hook_timeout_holds_both_waits under MEASURED_TIMEOUT_SECS 2,900 (measured 2026-11-23, hook2.log, D3000s2900 ran to its end and rewoke)
decisions.why: Mechanism needed for the wait above, held under a measured run; the task line asked to measure the cap and design within it, and it was measured (10 s and 1,200 s enforced as set; 2,000, 2,900 and 3,700 s runs completed and rewoke). No narrowing.

decisions.summary: When live work is still going at the check's deadline, the check exits 2 with one short notice ('IDLE CHECK: N builder(s) still working past its wait. End the turn; the next Stop re-arms the check.', each builder's id and description) instead of exiting silently
decisions.why: Presumed not legitimate: the approved proposal says the check is 'silent while the session is active or waiting on a tracked agent', and this speaks while a builder is working. It passes on MODE 1's third route: silence here would defeat the request's own purpose, concretely. The check exists to speak 'when it is idle with actionable work'; a hook cannot outlive its timeout (measured 2026-11-23: enforced as set), and only the hook's own exit 2 wakes the session (hooks reference, read 2026-11-23; a detached successor cannot), so a silent exit at the deadline ends all checking until some unrelated Stop. A builder whose unbounded background run (or a chain of runs) then stalls, the session silent, is never named - the session sits idle forever with actionable work, the exact defect this task fixes. The only way to keep a Stop-armed check alive is one wake; the notice is the minimum text for it (BREVITY-cut by message-check), and with the 2,400 s wait covering a Monitor's full cap it arises only for runs longer than that. The GM's own framing ('a cron that fires every 5 minutes') presumes a check that keeps firing; this is the only means here to keep it firing. Not a word-level carve-out: it serves the purpose rather than gutting it.

decisions.summary: The notice is said every time live work outlasts the wait, not once
decisions.why: Adjudicated separately, same route: each wake is a new check with the same physical limit, so saying it once and then exiting silently at the next deadline reintroduces the dead check and the never-named stalled builder. Repetition is the existence decision applied at every deadline, not a further departure.

decisions.summary: Cadence one notice per IDLE_SECS + WAIT_SECS (45 minutes, a CONVENTION) while a builder's run outlasts the wait
decisions.why: Not a separate departure: given the legitimate wake, how often it comes trades notice frequency against how late a stalled builder is named; a 4,000 s timeout was measured to run with no clamp found, so a longer cadence is available, but choosing among them is design and cost, not fidelity - the request fixes no cadence. The plan flags the cost to the GM ('the GM may cut it').

decisions.summary: The hand-on notice is outside make guard-messages' corpus (as T193's idle words are) and was judged by message-check on a hand-built bundle: FIDELITY passed, BREVITY cuts applied
decisions.why: The 2026-11-23 hook-output request asked for brevity with no loss of fidelity, reviewed by a subagent; the notice was so reviewed and cut. The corpus gap is an existing reach of a check, not a narrowing of this request, and it leaves no wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: After T193 (landed) and before T200; classed as performance work (removes false wakes, names a Monitor-length stall ~10 minutes after the watch ends instead of never)
decisions.why: Order follows the GM's 2026-11-20 rule that performance work comes first and the 2026-11-23 request that motivated the idle check; no scope beyond the defects named.

decisions.summary: a fixed error or questionable finding owes its round even on an unchanged sheet (e.g. fixed in the docs)
decisions.why: An error or questionable finding is a factual one; 'only factual findings cascade' is the GM's rule, so a factual fix owing a round is the rule applied, not a carve-out from it. The sheet being unchanged does not show the fix was right.

decisions.summary: a finding of no or an unknown severity owes a round, failing closed as T188 does
decisions.why: The standing rule exempts only findings shown to be non-factual; a finding whose class is unknown cannot be shown so, and failing closed keeps the GM's 'only factual findings cascade' from passing an unclassified factual finding.

decisions.summary: a nitpick fixed on the sheet owes only a change-scoped, adversarial building-review of the edit (make review-fixed UNIT= FINDING=, the kept reviewed sheet, T189's before/after pairs); a clean SCOPE=change verdict (PASS, every finding minor, gate not red) is carried by carried/answered/standing/checkpoint/push review gate
decisions.why: Directly the GM's words 'make only the smallest possible changes perhaps with some kind of adversarial subagent review process' and the approved rule 're-reviews scoped to the change'. The plan says plainly the saving is unmeasured and the rule is the GM's, which is correct framing.

decisions.summary: an error or questionable finding fixed on the sheet is refused by make review-fixed and owes the full round, not a change-scoped one
decisions.why: In tension with 're-reviews scoped to the change', which the section itself applies to building reviews, so it is ruled. Legitimate on the GM's own words: 'style edits are just a different category of thing than factual inaccuracies. And it might be that when we are cascading, we are only interested in factual inaccuracies' - the scoped route he proposed was for the small, non-factual edits, and a factual fix is the class he said matters. Purpose test: the oscillation the GM described was rounds driven by style findings; under this same section any nitpick the full round raises then stands (T199-standing) and, if fixed, owes only a scoped round, so the full round cannot restart the oscillation. Nor is it a defect left: a full review after a real-flaw fix is not a wrong outcome. Resting this on the request's words, not on T199's task line, which the bundle does not carry.

decisions.summary: a change-scoped round that is not clean (not PASS, a finding above minor, or its gate red) owes the full round
decisions.why: The adversarial scoped round exists to catch an edit that did more than the named fix or made something wrong; when it finds that, the change is no longer the small one the GM's scoped route covers, so falling back is the route working, not an exception to it.

decisions.summary: a verdict recorded before T199 (no kept reviewed sheet hashing to its content_key) owes the full round

It lapses on its own as verdicts are re-recorded.

### T201 Performance checklist (docs/performance-checklist.md - prompts, never a gate; time is the goal, calls the measure)

decisions.summary: stalls::in_progress names a builder only while its task is in progress: box open, started since its last landing (task-starts row after the last land end, or the active mark), not held by waits, not held by name by a binding ruling (holds::named), its feature not set down at or after its last start
decisions.why: The GM approved (2026-11-23) a periodic check that 'speaks only when it is idle with actionable work and respects binding rulings and set-downs'. A parked (set down since start), waiting, held-by-name, landed or never-started builder is not actionable work; naming it with a wake command is the wrong outcome the request was filed to end. Each condition carries a clause of the approved proposal; none narrows it.

decisions.summary: A ruling that holds NEW work (holds::held) does not hold a task already started, and a set-down BEFORE the task's start does not either: T184's builder, started 19:22:55Z under 451's new-work hold and after an 11:06:29Z set-down, is still named
decisions.why: 'Respects binding rulings and set-downs' is honored to each ruling's own reach: a hold on new work holds the tasks not yet started (the plan's statement of holds::held and T183; rulings.md carries no ruling text, so the hold's scope is taken from the plan). The request itself describes the offending block as a 'builder slot is free' prompt under a ruling 'that held new work' - i.e. a prompt to START work; naming a live builder of an already-started task starts nothing. A set-down before a later start is superseded by that start (active's own test). No ruling or set-down is overridden, so nothing is narrowed.

decisions.summary: WAIT_SECS 600 -> 2,400 s (MONITOR_SECS 1,800 measured + STALL_SECS 600 GUESS), so a watch that runs its full 30 minutes and ends unheard is named within one check
decisions.why: Fixes a defect in the approved check: a builder stalled after a Monitor that outlived the 600 s wait was never named, i.e. the check stayed silent while idle with actionable work, contrary to the request. A constant change serving the request.

decisions.summary: The Idle hook entry's timeout 960 -> 2,760 s (the two waits + 60 s reads, a CONVENTION), pinned by the_hook_timeout_holds_both_waits under MEASURED_TIMEOUT_SECS 2,900 (measured 2026-11-23, hook2.log, D3000s2900 ran to its end and rewoke)
decisions.why: Mechanism needed for the wait above, held under a measured run; the task line asked to measure the cap and design within it, and it was measured (10 s and 1,200 s enforced as set; 2,000, 2,900 and 3,700 s runs completed and rewoke). No narrowing.

decisions.summary: When live work is still going at the check's deadline, the check exits 2 with one short notice ('IDLE CHECK: N builder(s) still working past its wait. End the turn; the next Stop re-arms the check.', each builder's id and description) instead of exiting silently
decisions.why: Presumed not legitimate: the approved proposal says the check is 'silent while the session is active or waiting on a tracked agent', and this speaks while a builder is working. It passes on MODE 1's third route: silence here would defeat the request's own purpose, concretely. The check exists to speak 'when it is idle with actionable work'; a hook cannot outlive its timeout (measured 2026-11-23: enforced as set), and only the hook's own exit 2 wakes the session (hooks reference, read 2026-11-23; a detached successor cannot), so a silent exit at the deadline ends all checking until some unrelated Stop. A builder whose unbounded background run (or a chain of runs) then stalls, the session silent, is never named - the session sits idle forever with actionable work, the exact defect this task fixes. The only way to keep a Stop-armed check alive is one wake; the notice is the minimum text for it (BREVITY-cut by message-check), and with the 2,400 s wait covering a Monitor's full cap it arises only for runs longer than that. The GM's own framing ('a cron that fires every 5 minutes') presumes a check that keeps firing; this is the only means here to keep it firing. Not a word-level carve-out: it serves the purpose rather than gutting it.

decisions.summary: The notice is said every time live work outlasts the wait, not once
decisions.why: Adjudicated separately, same route: each wake is a new check with the same physical limit, so saying it once and then exiting silently at the next deadline reintroduces the dead check and the never-named stalled builder. Repetition is the existence decision applied at every deadline, not a further departure.

decisions.summary: Cadence one notice per IDLE_SECS + WAIT_SECS (45 minutes, a CONVENTION) while a builder's run outlasts the wait
decisions.why: Not a separate departure: given the legitimate wake, how often it comes trades notice frequency against how late a stalled builder is named; a 4,000 s timeout was measured to run with no clamp found, so a longer cadence is available, but choosing among them is design and cost, not fidelity - the request fixes no cadence. The plan flags the cost to the GM ('the GM may cut it').

decisions.summary: The hand-on notice is outside make guard-messages' corpus (as T193's idle words are) and was judged by message-check on a hand-built bundle: FIDELITY passed, BREVITY cuts applied
decisions.why: The 2026-11-23 hook-output request asked for brevity with no loss of fidelity, reviewed by a subagent; the notice was so reviewed and cut. The corpus gap is an existing reach of a check, not a narrowing of this request, and it leaves no wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: After T193 (landed) and before T200; classed as performance work (removes false wakes, names a Monitor-length stall ~10 minutes after the watch ends instead of never)
decisions.why: Order follows the GM's 2026-11-20 rule that performance work comes first and the 2026-11-23 request that motivated the idle check; no scope beyond the defects named.
